summary: Ticket to Ride: Europe is the accessible train-route family game where players collect colored cards to claim routes across a map, fulfilling secret destination tickets for points, spiced up with tunnels and ferries that add small extra costs and risk. It teaches in minutes and plays quickly, making it a reliable gateway game for mixed groups.
praised: extremely easy to teach and quick to play
satisfying tactile moment of claiming a route
tunnels and stations add welcome variety over the original map
criticised: luck of the ticket and card draws can swing outcomes
interaction is mostly indirect, limited to route blocking
little room for comeback once behind late game

interaction.kind: route blocking, otherwise parallel set collection
interaction.detail: Players share a single map of routes, so claiming a route you need before an opponent can is the main point of contact, but each player's hand of cards and completed tickets are private and otherwise played in parallel.

scoring.why: Points come from route length, completed (or failed) destination tickets, and a longest-route bonus, so the winner balances efficient route claims with well-chosen tickets.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by claiming a network of routes that completes your secret tickets while denying opponents key connections.
